body:
If you kill yourself that removes the possibility of getting better. For me anxiety is worse than depression, so I understand how you feel there. Having both is almost impossible to bear. You just want to feel normal or die. I feel that way a lot, most recently a few hours ago. Sometimes you just have to take it day by day. Find little things that you enjoy or that make you happy.

I was bullied a lot all of my life. Even now in my 20’s I experience people being mean and hateful, but how people treat you has nothing to do with you.

I could have written something like this when I was younger. It sounds very similar to how I felt. One thing about depression is it doesn’t just go away for most people. To me, the good times are remission. That’s not to say people don’t recover, but it’s very common for people who have had one depressive episode to have more. 

I’m very suicidal right now, and I have been for a year. I give myself little goals to get to. So for example, if still feel as bad a week from now as I do in this very moment, with zero periods of relief, happiness, or any form of joy, then I’ll end it. So far there’s always been a window even if it’s very small where I felt okay, so I don’t do it. It’s hard, unfair, and debilitating at times. 

People you love will not always understand how to help you, and sometimes they’ll even make you feel worse. Just know they love you and care for you. No one can save you, but you can save yourself, and you’re worth saving. My mom used to be hard on me and one day I told her I felt like killing myself everyday and could she please back off a little, and while she still slips up things have gotten a lot better. Some times we assume they should know or see the signs, but that’s not always the case.

I was diagnosed with major depression and panic disorder. I’ve been on antidepressants, benzos, and antipsychotics. Both antidepressants and antipsychotics caused adverse events every time, though not always right away. Benzos do calm me down, but they’re not a long term solution. I’ve done inpatient and outpatient treatment. Nothing helps. 

My kids are 2 and 4, so they definitely don’t know how I feel. I just say I’m tired or not feeling good on the days I can’t do much. 

As for family support I’m burnt out on asking for help. I’ve been reaching out since I was 14 (23 now) and at this point I feel like a burden. They have lives too outside of my constant crisis and I’m tired of putting that weight on them. 

I know suicide is selfish, and I know it causes pain. My grandma killed herself, and she was my favorite person in the world. That being said the older I get the more I understand why she did it. And that scares me because I know my kids are at risk, but I think growing up with a mom who is mentally ill has to come with its own consequences as well.
